title: Employment Situation (Jul 2027 data) — 08:30 ET, the year's largest payroll-day rates move and its smallest equity one
source: EST: derived from BLS's own published scheduling rule — the Employment Situation is released on the third Friday following the end of the reference week (the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th). THE RULE WAS RE-IMPLEMENTED AND RE-VALIDATED FROM SCRATCH BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-09) rather than inherited from the proposal: 7 for 7 against the four confirmed jobs-* entries on this calendar (2026-09-04, 2026-10-02, 2026-11-06, 2026-12-04) and the three historical Sunday-July-4 releases (2004-07-02, 2010-07-02, 2021-07-02). For July 2027 the reference week is Sun 2027-07-11 to Sat 2027-07-17, and the third Friday after 07-17 is 2027-08-06, an ordinary NYSE trading day with no holiday within a week of it, so the rule's one documented failure mode (a holiday landing on the rule's own Friday) cannot fire here. The prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov returned HTTP 403 to a browser user-agent on all four schedule routes re-tried on 2026-09-09 (/schedule/news_release/2027_sched.htm, /schedule/news_release/empsit.htm, /schedule/home.htm, /bls/news-release/empsit.htm) and fred.stlouisfed.org/release/dates?rid=50 returned 404 — all five recorded in this event's probe-ref.blocked. A derived date is not a published one
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-09), superseding proposals/jobs-2027-08-06.from-jobs-2027-07-02.json, which stays where it is and is now shadowed. WHAT THIS SESSION ESTABLISHED THAT THE PROPOSAL DID NOT. (1) THE HEADLINE STRUCTURAL FACT THE PROPOSAL LED WITH IS PREDICTIVELY WORTHLESS. 'First payroll after an FOMC' was tested three independent ways over 392 payroll releases 1993-2026, against scheduled FOMC decision dates parsed from federalreserve.gov's own historical pages: post-FOMC vs pre-FOMC print-day |move| (16 tests, one nominal hit at p=0.049 that does not reproduce), the sharper >=35-days-from-next-decision cut that literally matches 2027-08-06 (all null), and Spearman rho of daysToNextFOMC against |move| (all |rho| <= 0.12, all p > 0.07). Where a payroll sits in the FOMC cycle does not predict how much it moves anything. (2) WHAT SURVIVES IS A CALENDAR-MONTH FACT, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST IN THE FAMILY. Measured on Yahoo split/dividend-adjusted daily bars 1993-2026, the payroll-day amplification ratio (payroll-session median |move| over the SAME month's non-payroll-session median) ranks August 1st of 12 for TLT 2.03x, IEF 2.36x and AGG 2.32x against a median month of 1.46x/1.45x/1.57x -- and the numerator carries it, not a quiet denominator: August's payroll-session median is the year's highest in all three (TLT 1.024%, IEF 0.589%, AGG 0.338%) while every month's non-payroll baseline is flat within noise. The same table ranks August 9th of 12 for SPY at 1.04x -- the August payroll is the year's least equity-relevant one (0.490% vs February's 1.058%). (3) THE SUMMER-FRAGILITY STORY IS REFUTED. August payroll sessions clear the all-payroll 95th percentile |SPY move| 1 time in 33 against ~1.7 expected; 2024-08-02 ranks only 5th among them; forward 10-session realized vol is 12.02% vs 12.66% for other months; and volume runs 1.15x trailing-20, indistinguishable from any other payroll. (4) IT IS ALONE: zero tracked events within 5 days, the only scheduled item between fomc-2027-07-28 (D-9) and fomc-minutes-2027-08-18 (D+12). (5) federalreserve.gov's own 2027 FOMC calendar was RETRIEVABLE this session (HTTP 200, page-stated 'Last Update: August 19, 2026') and names July 27-28 and September 14-15 -- a FED: primary that corroborates fomc-2027-07-28 and fomc-2027-09-15, both currently carried as estimate by their own lanes. Not amended here: one file per owner (#1449). Impact high and symbols [] match every other jobs-* entry. Estimates widen caution and license no entry.
